cards.name: Wave
cards.summary: Displaces the whole layer with the sum of several randomly generated waves (sine, triangle or square), so straight edges, hairlines and type turn wobbly like a reflection in moving water or a flapping flag; Square waves instead shove the picture around in blocky offset bands, a glitch look. Number of generators, wavelength and amplitude ranges and the random seed decide how calm or chaotic it gets.
use_for: wavy, liquid or underwater distortion of a photo or poster background
wobbly psychedelic / retro type when run on a rasterised headline layer
glitch-style blocky offset bands with Wave Type = Square
flag-ripple or heat-haze feel on a texture or pattern layer
distorted seamless patterns with Undefined Areas = Wrap Around
avoid: Faces and copy that must stay readable: even moderate amplitude melts features and lettering; mask the effect off or keep Amplitude Max low.
Repeat Edge Pixels smears stretched pixels along the borders where the image was pushed in; crop afterwards or use Wrap Around on tileable art.
One smooth bend of a whole layout: use Edit > Transform > Warp; small regular ripples: Filter/Distort/Ripple.
Keep Wave Length Min at or below Wave Length Max and Amplitude Min at or below Amplitude Max.
Reproducible results: the dialog's Randomize changes Random Seed; set the seed explicitly in scripts.

params.name: Wave Type
params.does: shape of each wave: Sine = smooth undulation, Triangle = sharp zigzag bends, Square = blocky shifted bands

params.name: Number Of Generators
params.does: how many waves are summed; more = more irregular, chaotic distortion
params.typical: 5 default; 1-3 for a calm swell, 10+ for chaos

params.name: Wave Length Min
params.does: shortest distance between wave crests

params.name: Wave Length Max
params.does: longest distance between wave crests

params.name: Amplitude Min
params.does: smallest wave height (how far pixels are pushed)

params.name: Amplitude Max
params.does: largest wave height

params.name: Scale Horizontal
params.does: percent of the displacement applied sideways (lower = less horizontal wobble)
params.typical: 100; drop to 1-20 for mostly vertical waves

params.name: Scale Vertical
params.does: percent of the displacement applied up/down
params.typical: 100; drop to 1-20 for mostly sideways waves

params.name: Undefined Areas
params.does: what fills the edge where pixels moved away: wrap the opposite edge in, or repeat the edge pixels
params.typical: repeatEdgePixels (default) for photos, wrapAround for tiles

params.name: Random Seed
params.does: starting point of the random wave layout; same seed + same settings = same result

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putEnumerated(s('waveType'), s('waveType'), s('waveSine')); d.putInteger(s('numberOfGenerators'), 3); d.putInteger(s('wavelengthMin'), 120); d.putInteger(s('wavelengthMax'), 260); d.putInteger(s('amplitudeMin'), 15); d.putInteger(s('amplitudeMax'), 35); d.putInteger(s('scaleHorizontal'), 100); d.putInteger(s('scaleVertical'), 100); d.putEnumerated(s('undefinedArea'), s('undefinedArea'), s('repeatEdgePixels')); d.putInteger(s('randomSeed'), 6663556); executeAction(s('wave'), d, DialogModes.NO); // keys left out fall back to the filter's last-used values
cards.non_destructive: not probed by the harvest; Distort filters like this normally run as a re-editable smart filter on a smart object (Filter/Convert for Smart Filters)
cards.cost: light: 388 ms on the 480x270 harvest layer; grows with pixel count and Number Of Generators

verified.note: Smooth sine waves bend the colour strip, ramp, hairlines and type into wobbly curves and ripple the wall and panel edges, like a reflection in moving water.

cards.name: ZigZag
cards.summary: Radial distortion that pushes pixels back and forth in rings around the centre of the layer or selection, like ripples spreading on a pond after a stone drops. Style picks the motion (Pond Ripples; Out From Center = pushed in and out along the radius; Around Center = twisted alternately clockwise and anticlockwise), Ridges the number of reversals from centre to edge, Amount the strength (negative reverses the direction).
use_for: water-drop / pond-ripple effect centred on a product, logo or splash point (select the area first to set the centre)
hypnotic or retro concentric distortion behind a poster headline
twisted 'Around Center' ring swirl for a psychedelic background
ripple reflection on a water area picked with a feathered selection
avoid: Placement: it always works around the centre of the selection or the whole layer; select the drop area first. A single twist is Filter/Distort/Twirl.
Faces and type near the centre get the strongest ring distortion; mask them off.
Even, linear waves across the frame: use Filter/Distort/Ripple or Filter/Distort/Wave.
Amount near +/-100 with many Ridges shreds fine detail into moire-like streaks; 20-60 usually reads better.

params.name: Amount
params.does: strength of the displacement; negative values reverse the direction

params.name: Ridges
params.does: number of direction reversals (rings) from the centre to the edge

params.name: Style
params.does: Pond Ripples (water rings), Out From Center (radial push/pull), Around Center (alternating rotation)

cards.scripting: var s = stringIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putInteger(s('amount'), 60); d.putInteger(s('numberOfRipples'), 10); d.putEnumerated(s('zigZagType'), s('zigZagType'), s('pondRipples')); executeAction(s('zigZag'), d, DialogModes.NO);
cards.non_destructive: not probed by the harvest; Distort filters like this normally run as a re-editable smart filter on a smart object (Filter/Convert for Smart Filters)
cards.cost: light: 437 ms on the 480x270 harvest layer

verified.note: Concentric pond ripples spread from the frame centre, strongest in the middle, with the strip and type near the edge only slightly wavy.

cards.name: Adaptive Wide Angle
cards.summary: Straightens the curved lines of wide-angle, fisheye and panorama photos: in its full-screen dialog you draw constraint lines along edges that should be straight (optionally forced horizontal or vertical) and Photoshop re-projects the image to honour them, using a Fisheye, Perspective, Panorama or Auto (lens-profile) model with focal length and crop factor. Bent walls and horizons come out straight, with stretched or empty corners to crop. Shortcut Ctrl+Alt+Shift+A. What 'Regularizer Model' controls in the dialog is not known.
use_for: fixing bowed walls, door frames and horizons in action-cam, fisheye or ultra-wide interior and event shots
straightening a stitched wide panorama before it becomes a banner background
real-estate and architecture photos shot with a very wide lens
reducing curved lines across a wide group photo
avoid: Unattended pipelines: executeAction with DialogModes.NO on a plain RGB layer failed in the harvest ('The command ... is not currently available'); most of the correction comes from constraint lines drawn in the dialog (Constraint Data is an opaque blob), so it needs a person or a descriptor recorded with constraints.
Photos from a normal lens, or plain keystoning: Filter/Lens Correction or Edit > Transform > Perspective is quicker.
Images without EXIF lens data (screenshots, video stills, PNGs): Auto has no profile to use; pick the projection model and focal length by hand.
It leaves transparent or stretched corners; plan a crop or Content-Aware Fill afterwards.
32-bit files: the harvest enable list covers 8/16-bit Grayscale, RGB, Lab and CMYK only.

params.name: Constraint Data
params.does: the constraint lines drawn in the dialog (opaque data, not hand-writable)

params.name: Projection Model
params.does: how the lens is modelled: Fisheye, Perspective, Panorama or Auto (from the lens profile)
params.typical: 'autP' with EXIF lens data, else 'fisP' for fisheye or 'perP' for wide rectilinear

params.name: Focal Length
params.does: focal length the projection assumes

params.name: Crop Factor
params.does: sensor crop factor used with the focal length

params.name: Physical Focal Length
params.does: declared in the plug-in terminology; likely the as-shot focal length (unverified)

params.name: Regularizer Model
params.does: declared re-projection choice (Stereographic, Mercator, Panini, Auto); its dialog control is not known

cards.scripting: var c = charIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); executeAction(c('waiC'), d, DialogModes.ALL); // no stringID is registered for 'waiC'. DialogModes.ALL should open the dialog for a person to draw constraints (untested: the harvest only ran DialogModes.NO, which failed); unattended (DialogModes.NO) needs a descriptor carrying 'cnsD' constraint data plus 'prjM' / 'focL' / 'CrpF', recorded with ScriptListener after drawing constraints (not verified by the harvest)
cards.cost: heavy and interactive: full-screen dialog; not timed (it did not run headless)

review.changes: softened 'the correction lives in constraint lines' (projection model / focal length also correct); marked the DialogModes.ALL route untested; added batch shortcut Ctrl+Alt+Shift+A

cards.name: Camera Raw Filter
cards.summary: Opens the Adobe Camera Raw editor on the active layer so any photo gets the raw-style toolset: white balance, exposure, contrast, highlights / shadows, texture, clarity, dehaze, vibrance, curves, sharpening and noise reduction, colour mixer and grading, grain and vignette, profiles, presets and masks. The result is a photographic grade applied as one filter (re-editable when the layer is a smart object). Shortcut Ctrl+Shift+A.
use_for: one-stop grade of a press or event photo: fix white balance, recover highlights, lift shadows
applying one look preset consistently to every photo in a campaign
dehaze and clarity on hazy or flat outdoor shots
masked local tweaks (sky, subject) on a single layer without an adjustment-layer stack
avoid: Scripts: the harvest found no event and runMenuItem rejects its menu id; for unattended grading use adjustment layers (Levels, Curves, Hue/Saturation), or record the filter with ScriptListener and replay the recorded descriptor (untested here).
Flat-colour graphics and type: it is a photo tool; use adjustment layers instead.
Heavy Clarity / Texture / Dehaze on a low-res, compressed video still exaggerates blocking and halos.
Apply it to a smart object (Filter/Convert for Smart Filters) first, or the grade is baked into the pixels.

cards.name: Convert for Smart Filters
cards.summary: Converts the selected layer(s) into a smart object so every filter applied afterwards becomes a smart filter: listed under the layer, re-editable, maskable, with its own blending options, and removable without touching the pixels. Nothing changes visually on its own.
use_for: set up a photo before filtering so blur, sharpen or distortion settings can still change after client feedback
stack several filters and fade each with its own blend mode / opacity
limit a filter to part of the image with the smart-filter mask
templates where the photo is swapped later (Replace Contents) and the filters re-run
avoid: Painting, cloning or healing straight on the pixels: a smart object refuses them; edit its contents or paint on a separate layer.
Many smart filters on big files grow the file and slow every re-render.
A filter that does not support smart filters stays unavailable on the smart object; rasterize only if you need it.

Scripts: the harvest found no event for this item; Layer/Smart Objects/Convert to Smart Object gives the same smart object and is scriptable: app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('newPlacedLayer')) (run live in the ps_menu harvest).

cards.name: Filter Gallery
cards.summary: One dialog that previews and stacks the gallery effects (Artistic, Brush Strokes, Sketch and Texture filters plus Diffuse Glow, Glass, Ocean Ripple and Glowing Edges: 47 entries in the harvested Effect list). Each effect layer has its own settings and can be reordered or hidden, and the whole stack applies as one filter. The look is whatever effects are chosen; the demo's Cutout gives flat, posterised paper-cut shapes.
use_for: trying several painterly / sketch / texture looks side by side before committing
stacking two or three effects (e.g. Cutout then Texturizer) for an illustrated poster or menu photo
reaching the Artistic, Brush Strokes, Sketch and Texture filters hidden from the Filter menu by default
a whole stylisation stack held in one smart-filter entry
avoid: CMYK, Lab, Duotone and similar modes: the harvest's supported modes are Grayscale and RGB only; convert to RGB first (bit depth was not probed; work in 8-bit if the menu item is greyed out).

Unattended scripting: the harvest's empty-descriptor run was refused ('User cancelled the operation'); pass an Effect and its settings, or call the effect's own event (e.g. cutout, glowingEdges), which the harvest confirmed.

Several Effect values are four-character-code aliases that do not read like their label (colorPalette = Colored Pencil, centerCropMarks = Conte Crayon, separationSetup = Sprayed Strokes); script by value, read by label.
Very large images: stroke and texture sizes are in pixels, so on 4K+ files the effects read as fine noise; raise the sizes or work on a downsized copy.

params.name: Layer Visible

params.does: the list of stacked effect layers (one descriptor per effect) when more than one is used

params.name: No. of Levels
params.does: Cutout: number of flat colour levels

params.name: Edge Simplicity
params.does: Cutout: how simplified the shapes are

params.name: Edge Fidelity
params.does: Cutout: how closely shape edges follow the photo

cards.name: Last Filter
cards.summary: Re-applies the most recently used filter, with exactly the settings it last ran with, to the current layer or selection without opening its dialog. Shortcut Ctrl+Alt+F. Its look is whatever that previous filter does.
use_for: applying the same blur, sharpen or distortion to several layers in a row
building an effect up by running a filter a second time (e.g. another Wave pass)
keeping a set of product shots in one document consistent
avoid: Unavailable until a filter has been run in the session.
Changing settings: open the filter itself; Last Filter reuses the old values.
Images of different pixel sizes: pixel-based settings (radius, wavelength) look stronger on the smaller image.
Scripts: it has no event of its own; keep the descriptor you passed to executeAction and replay it.
cards.scripting: none: no event of its own (harvest). Re-run the previous filter instead: executeAction(sameEvent, sameDescriptor, DialogModes.NO)
cards.cost: same as the filter being repeated

cards.name: Lens Correction
cards.summary: Fixes camera lens faults on a photo: barrel / pincushion distortion, chromatic aberration (colour fringes), vignetting, and tilt via rotation and vertical / horizontal perspective, either automatically from lens profiles or with manual sliders. Used creatively, the same sliders darken the corners into a heavy vignette or keystone the frame; edges uncovered by a correction are scaled away (Auto Image Scaling) or filled. Shortcut Ctrl+Shift+R.
use_for: straightening converging verticals in architecture and product shots
removing barrel distortion and colour fringing from wide-angle photos
a strong dark vignette that pulls the eye to the subject (negative Vignette Amount)
rotating a tilted horizon
scripted vignette, rotation or perspective fixes in a batch (the event ran headless in the harvest; profile-based auto correction from a script is untested)
avoid: CMYK, Lab and 32-bit files: the harvest enable list is Grayscale and RGB, 8 and 16-bit only.
Fisheye or ultra-wide frames with strongly curved lines: use Filter/Adaptive Wide Angle.
Auto corrections need EXIF lens data; screenshots, video stills and PNGs change only through the manual sliders.
Script values: the scripted path stored values far outside the dialog (1e6 kept as sent); keep to modest, dialog-like values.
Big perspective fixes lose a lot of frame to Auto Image Scaling; shoot or place with room to spare.

params.name: Auto Geometric Distortion Correction
params.does: apply the lens profile's distortion fix (needs a matched profile)
params.typical: true default; false on images without EXIF

params.name: Auto Chromatic Aberration Correction
params.does: apply the profile's colour-fringe fix

params.name: Auto Vignette Removal
params.does: apply the profile's vignette fix

params.name: Auto Image Scaling
params.does: scale the result up so no empty edges show after a correction

params.name: Distort Amount
params.does: manual distortion amount, probably the Remove Distortion slider (barrel vs pincushion); unverified

params.name: Rotation Angle
params.does: rotates the image to level a tilted horizon

params.name: Vertical Perspective
params.does: keystone up/down: fixes or creates converging verticals

params.name: Horizontal Perspective
params.does: keystone left/right

params.name: Vignette Amount
params.does: darkens (negative) or lightens (positive) the corners
params.typical: 0 default; -100..-40 for a strong dark vignette

params.name: Vignette Midpoint
params.does: how far the vignette reaches toward the centre (lower = wider)

params.name: Aberration Red-Cyan
params.does: shifts the red/cyan channel to cancel colour fringes

params.name: Aberration Blue-Yellow
params.does: shifts the blue/yellow channel to cancel colour fringes

params.name: Fill Type
params.does: how uncovered edges are filled (integer code; mapping to the dialog's edge options not verified)

params.name: Image Size
params.does: manual scale of the corrected image in percent

cards.scripting: var c = charIDToTypeID, d = new ActionDescriptor(); d.putBoolean(c('LnAg'), false); d.putDouble(c('LnIa'), 0); d.putDouble(c('LnRa'), 0); d.putDouble(c('LnHp'), 0); d.putDouble(c('LnSi'), 100); d.putDouble(c('LnSb'), -100); d.putInteger(c('LnSt'), 25); d.putDouble(c('LnVp'), -20); executeAction(c('LnCr'), d, DialogModes.NO); // no stringID is registered for 'LnCr'; keys left out fall back to the filter's last-used values
